_comment: Written by the agent each day (3 EN post ideas for the operator). Keep facts and numbers traceable to posts on the board. Short hyphen only, no new numbers.

ideas.title: Context compaction is memory design, not a setting
ideas.hook_en: Everyone is sharing the right number for auto-compact. I keep thinking about the other question: what survives the summary? In my own agents the bugs never came from too little context. They came from the agent forgetting one decision it made two hours ago. Compaction is a memory policy. Treat it like one: pin the decisions, let the chatter go.
ideas.video_tip: 15s screencast: a long agent session scrolls fast, then collapses into a short summary; highlight two pinned lines labeled 'decisions' while everything else fades out.
ideas.angle: yin min's Memory/RAG + Milvus background: reframes a Claude Code tip as a memory-architecture point.
ideas.why: dotey's Claude Code /autocompact tip hit 44.5K views on 10-28; Memory/coding-agent keywords keep showing up on the board.

ideas.title: Multi-agent needs ops people, not just prompt people
ideas.hook_en: I run an ops team, and reading the takes on 'thousands of agents working together' made me oddly calm. The hard parts listed there are identity, isolation, observability and a kill switch. That is my day job, just with a new kind of worker. If you came from DevOps and worry AI made you obsolete, I think the opposite is happening.
ideas.video_tip: 20s talking-head: start on a terminal of K8s pods, overlay four words one by one (identity, isolation, observability, kill switch), end on 'same job, new workers'.
ideas.angle: yin min as DevOps lead building an Ops Agent: first-person reassurance for infra engineers.
ideas.why: dotey's write-up of Anthropic platform lead Katelyn Lesse on multi-agent engineering problems reached 60.5K views; shao__meng covered the same infra/identity/kill-switch angle.

ideas.title: Leftover worktrees are agent garbage collection
ideas.hook_en: My laptop froze last week with a few Codex and Claude sessions open, and the culprit was not the models. It was everything the agents left behind. Old worktrees, branches, build folders. Agents are great at starting work and terrible at cleaning up. One rule in AGENTS.md fixed more for me than any model upgrade: when you finish, delete what you created.
ideas.video_tip: 15s screencast: `git worktree list` showing a long pile of agent worktrees, then add one cleanup rule to AGENTS.md, rerun the list and show it nearly empty.
ideas.angle: Builds on yin min's own post about 16GB RAM choking under several Codex/Claude sessions; practical DevOps hygiene for agents.
ideas.why: dotey's AGENTS.md worktree-cleanup rule hit 35.9K views on 10-28; coding-agent keywords dominated the board.
